prompt: A clinic randomly assigns $100$ patients to a reminder-text program and $100$ to no reminders. Of the text group, $40$ show up for their checkup; of the control group, $30$ show up. Compute the chi-square statistic for the $2 \times 2$ table (showed up / did not, by group). Round to two decimal places.
hint: Chi-square needs expected counts, and those come from the overall show-up rate. How many of the $200$ patients showed up in total?

hints.text: Chi-square needs expected counts, and those come from the overall show-up rate. How many of the $200$ patients showed up in total?

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: if 20 of 40 total showed up, split evenly across two groups of 20, you would expect 10 shows and 10 no-shows in each group. Same logic with 70 of 200.

With $70$ of $200$ showing up, expect $35$ shows and $65$ no-shows in each group. The four terms are $\frac{(40-35)^2}{35}$, $\frac{(60-65)^2}{65}$, $\frac{(30-35)^2}{35}$ and $\frac{(70-65)^2}{65}$. Add them.
$0.714 + 0.385 + 0.714 + 0.385 \approx 2.20$, so the chi-square statistic is about $2.20$.

explanation: Observed: text group 40 show / 60 no-show; control 30 show / 70 no-show. Column totals: 70 show, 130 no-show; each row has 100.
Expected in every cell: $\frac{100 \times 70}{200} = 35$ shows and $\frac{100 \times 130}{200} = 65$ no-shows. Every observed cell is 5 away from expected.

$\chi^2 = 2 \times \frac{25}{35} + 2 \times \frac{25}{65} = 1.429 + 0.769 \approx 2.20$, with df $= (2-1)(2-1) = 1$. That is below the critical value $3.841$, so at $\alpha = 0.05$ the texts are not shown to help.

alternativeExplanations.title: Compare with a two-proportion z-test
steps: The same data as a $z$-test: $\hat{p}_1 = 0.40$, $\hat{p}_2 = 0.30$, pooled $0.35$, SE $= \sqrt{0.35 \times 0.65 \times 0.02} \approx 0.0674$, so $z \approx 1.48$.
Both tests give the same two-sided $p$-value (about $0.14$).
